>>>>> eternal recurrence # 24 802 691

It was almost time. Khaslana hastily removed Dawnmaker lodged inside the titankin in front of him, killing the last of its group that was running after a group of children. The monster disintegrated into small red blocks before fully disappearing.

“Get away from here,” He breathed out from his mask. “More are coming.”

All the kids nodded in unison, fear still etched on their small faces and freezing in place–just as afraid of the black robed swordsman in front of them.

“Go!” He didn’t have the patience to look after them, and with a little scare, the kids went running far from him.

From the nearby trees, crimson blocks can be seen slowly eating them away, spreading from one object to another like a virus. In tandem with the surge in number of black tide creatures, it was a definite sign of the prophecy nearing its fulfillment once again–the Chrysos heirs accomplishing the retrieval of the 12 coreflames to bring in the Era Nova they believed in.

It was time to meet them again…and watch them go once more. He used to attempt having discussions, but it proved time and time again to be futile, so he has turned to letting time run its course; only serving as a catalyst to speed up the process and meeting with the current cycle’s deliverer at the end, completing the cycle into a new one.

On his way, he heard a couple of noises–seemed like humans from a few words he could pick up. It came from the large rundown ruins near him. All the coreflames in his body were slowly chipping away at his sanity little by little, but with the small grasp he still had left of his humanity, the deliverer role he instilled in himself for millions of cycles cannot just stand still and ignore anyone who might be in need of help. If they didn’t pose any threat towards his mission, then they didn’t deserve his flames.

He hid his presence by a nearby surviving column to scout around. It was a group of soldiers from Okhema, evident from their armor. Must be a mission from Aglaea; the men collecting treasures before heading back home. Remembering his own memories of also doing such, he shut his eyes close, and shook his head. There was really no point in reminiscing. He was about to quickly take his leave when he heard a way too familiar name being called. Habits truly die hard when he also found himself stopping in his tracks. 

“Lord Phainon, are Kremnoans really into reading such old scriptures?” A soldier asked. From where Khaslana stood, he could see the number of soldiers surrounding another–one standing tall in the center with the clouds in his head. He could only see the man’s back–probably busy with reviewing the texts in front of him. “It’s quite hard to believe they would even have the time to read when most of them are such mindless brutes!”

Khaslana didn’t expect to come across this man right here. And this early too–so this was indeed a mission from Aglaea. He didn’t bother trying to figure out which this one could be in his memories. But from the soldier’s words, his ears perked up, and with the countless of Phainons resting in him, it was already second nature to need to defend a certain crown prince and his people’s honor. Of course, the very Phainon of this cycle would be the same.

“Don’t let your prejudices cloud your judgement, soldier!” A familiar light, and welcoming tone rang in Khaslana’s ears as the voice spoke. “The crown prince of Kremnos enjoys deciphering such old literature. He might not be the best at expressing himself with words, but I can assure you, his principles and views are as rich as any classics you may find!”

Khaslana’s brows furrowed–hearing his own words of praise for another man from another point of view was actually… quite off-putting with how enthusiastic he sounds. Has he always been like this?

“Ah… I see,” The soldier nodded awkwardly. “I apologize for my previous sentiment…”

“No need to apologize to me! Let me see that other book…”

It took until parting hour of just looking through different books, before Phainon decided he had enough to bring home. Khaslana watched the man easily carry a stack of old, dusty, worn down books wrapped together with a rope in both hands–laughing and sharing stories with the soldiers as they made their way back to the caravan. His white uniform was even dirtied, darkened at most of the edges. Has he no respect for Aglaea’s work? 

Khaslana wondered… based on the man’s words, he was taking those books home for… Mydeimos? So this must be one of those cycles. He felt the light pang in his chest, and ignored it–strongly refusing to acknowledge the memories that tried to resurface in his mind. Memories that weren't even his own.

He followed behind closely, careful to not get caught. And his initial guess was right. While the other soldiers were still preparing, Phainon was busy on his teleslate; excitement evident in his voice for the day’s spoils and the gifts he were bringing home

“ Hks , just get home safely,” A low and strong familiar voice huffed from the other line.

“Are you not going to wait for me?”

“No, I’m tired,” The voice replied, and Khaslana visibly cringed from how the white dog pouted from where he was. But it was as if the man from the other line also saw it. “Stop whining. I’ll come to you first thing in the morning.”

The man was quick to brighten up, a large puffy tail wagging on his back, “Alright! Yay!”

Before the group left, Phainon asked the soldiers to standby for a moment while he did one last lookout. Of course, the man was as sharp as always; coming face to face with his mortal enemy.

“It’s… it’s you…!” Phainon exclaimed, brandishing his claymore at that instant, and pointing it at the black robed swordsman that took his home away from him. “Step down! What do you want!?”

Khaslana only let out a breath before the two started clashing swords, going deeper into the confines of the large tall trees in the dark. Tails of light sparked with every kiss of metal, loud tinkering sounds scratching their ears at every embrace, and the two bouncing back on their feet from the magnitude of their strengths. Every fiber of their being was screaming, shouting, begging themselves to stop, but they kept going. It’s too early for their meeting–for Phainon to win nor for Khaslana to claim his rest.

No matter who won this duel, it both ends the same way–Khaslana receiving Phainon’s memories, and Phainon acquiring Khaslana’s. But if they were to become one this early on, when push comes to shove, the one to deliver the final blow to his companions will be as Phainon , and not as the Flame Reaver. Not that it changes anything nor it lightens the weight of the blood that stains his hands. 

The repercussions of this folly can no longer be negotiated when one sword stabs another, a uniform is donned and discards another, and memories come together in a smooth batter mixture, its contents indecipherable from one another. How many cycles has it been? Could he still actually keep track of which Phainons won? Of which Khaslanas lost? He is Phainon. He is Khaslana. Even he himself was not sure of the answer, but there was no other choice but to keep moving.

He stared at his reflection on the pond, his face wet and dripping with water as he tried to refresh his senses, but it was the very same darkened blue eyes that stared back at him.

“Lord Phainon?” A soldier came running, his steps slowing down to catch his breath. “I thought we heard some fighting! We’re ready to go…”

“It’s been taken care of. Let’s go.”

It was obvious that the soldier wanted to inquire further but Phainon had already led the way. The ride back to Okhema was long and quiet. In his memories, he would already have started conversations, and arranged the details for their follow-up report to Aglaea– but his head was just in a jumbled mess to think about anything straight. The soldiers could feel the absolute change in mood, and let their leader sink in his thoughts. He didn’t necessarily obtain a coreflame at the moment, but the surging warmth in his own body felt new. Would he burn those who come close to him? Maybe it was because of this cycle’s Phainon’s memories that added into the mix, that the feeling of novelty also came with it. It felt like he knew everything and nothing all at once.

Everything was mostly the same to how every other cycle went; almost like a blueprint to his life–to the flamechase journey–except for a few varieties here and there. Just as his teachers will always be his teachers or his friends will always be his friends; his relationships remain the same for every new Phainon that is born into the cycle. A new Phainon that was forced to watch to lose his companions every time, and for Khaslana to replay it over and over again.

Then there was also the crown prince of Kremnos, Mydeimos the Undying– his foe, rival, friend, companion… and most of all, his equal. As if fate was laughing right at his face, he had to take over a Phainon who happened to have built a much more intimate relationship with the prince. Such were many cases in a number of cycles.

As he entered his own room, with the stack of books in tow with him, he noticed the one thing that stood out from the room that he has basically already memorized for millions of times. In his side table was a large plate, covered with a clear wrap and a note taped on it; a layered cake with an assortment of fruits on top visible from the plastic. Utensils and small plates were on the side.

Welcome back!

-Mydei

He placed the books on the side of his bed, removed the upper accessories of his armor, and then took off his coat; leaving him in his black undershirt, before sitting down in front of the table. It was a cake made for him. There were even small drawings of an orange and gray chimera that Mydei loved to draw in the note. Was it really for him? Was it his Phainon that came back home safely? Will Mydei know?

All of his questions went out the window, as he felt that same sweetness melt on his tongue. Mydei loved to cook and bake for all the heirs, and as his closest companion, Phainon always had the privilege to taste test and even add his own ideas into the mix as a knowledgeable cook himself. Phainon simply liked the idea of having someone else cook for him, even if he questioned Mydei’s abilities when his food tasted suspicious at times. Whether it was Khaslana or Phainon, he would always love whatever Mydei had made for him.

During the very first cycle, despite starting off on the wrong foot, Phainon and Mydei still managed to grow close and fond of each other to a certain degree none of them were willing to acknowledge nor bring up. They were content with what they already had and shared–a quiet surrender and acceptance of their roles amd responsibilities as part of the flamechase journey– never more and nothing less . But the existence of Khaslana as the Flame Reaver in the next succeeding cycles meant that there was a new catalyst to push Phainon to new heights–to an aggressive test of his limits, his obsession with his physical and intellectual growth, and the desperation to prove himself. And in turn, also made him push the boundaries with the man who always received him with an equal burning passion–pushing into what they could have been more if it weren’t for their circumstances.

Phainon tossed and turned in his bed, not sleeping a wink from the new memories that bugged him until it was entry hour– his teleslate was already notifying him of his schedules for today. Might as well get ready, since Mydei will be visiting soon. He had showered in his private bath, and changed into the inner garments of his daily wear. Leaning down on the sink with his head down, he watched the droplets of water fall from his hair. After a while, he brushed all his hair back and ran his hands over his face– feeling a harrowing emptiness in his chest. Looking in the mirror, his skin was pale, a bit flushed from the warm temperature of the shower, or maybe just his burning body in general, and dark circles underneath his eyes. He spread his lips into his usual bright smile, then with teeth, and kept them on until he felt the strain on his cheeks. He was going to be the Deliverer everyone knew, the bright and charming hero of Amphoreus. He is Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.

The sudden knock on his door made him jump, and he went scrambling out of the restroom–trying to fix the bed and the clothes he left, while also drying his hair with his towel. Before he was ready, the door already opened and the person on the other side invited themselves in. He almost choked in his own saliva when he saw that Mydei was still in his tunic, his whole arm and legs exposed, those crimson lines drawing one’s attention to what could be hidden underneath those fabrics; hair and body moist as if he also just came from the baths– and the smell of fruits immediately occupying the air.

“M-Mydei, you’re early!” Phainon placed his hand by his nape, feeling his face heat up, not knowing what to do with the walking temptation in front of him.

“I said I will be coming in the morning,” Mydei’s brow raised, and searched around the room, his eyes landing on the covered plate on the table.

“Did you not like it? I asked the guards, and didn’t expect you’d be that late. The cake tastes better served cold, so it might have gone warm already when you arrived…”

“No, no, no! It was great. I… I was just saving it…” Phainon trailed off, when Mydei now looked at him in confusion. 

Did he say something wrong? Was Phainon not supposed to say that? The longing in his heart got the best of him last night, and decided to save some to last a few more days, like how he wanted to savor and prolong these moments of respite he stole from this cycle’s Phainon. He knew he was going to suffer for it nonetheless– might as well enjoy it while it lasted, right?

“I spoke to Aglaea beforehand and requested to grant you a well-deserved day-off for today. You just came home too, anyway…” Mydei looked away, and Phainon pursed his lips seeing the faint red dusting the prince’s cheeks.

What has this cycle’s Phainon been doing to have Mydei become this… soft … and this comfortable around him? Many other Phainons boast a similar experience with such a Mydei, numerous flashbacks ready to resurface in the back of Khaslana’s mind, but experiencing it first-hand was still different all together. Mydei, who had as many walls up as Phainon did, but they were able to find this level of comfort with one another… Maybe if he had more time… if he tried to breach those walls just a little bit more during the original cycle…

“Ah, I see that's great…” He didn’t know why he felt like an antsy awkward teenager spending his first time alone in a room with his partner. Or maybe there was also a semblance of truth in those words. And to add, with the amount of skin the man was showing–not that it was that different from how Mydei usually dresses, but in such comfortable clothes? As if they were already in that stage of a married couple, enjoying lazy idle times together.

Phainon coughed, and adjusted the choker on his neck, trying to cool down the sweat dripping down from his neck. He turned his back and went to grab his bag to show the books he got. Mydei was here for those anyways; might as well get things done before he does something to add more on the many things he will be regretting once this is all over.

“I got you a couple of books–" His words were cut off when he felt the warmth spread around his back, and firm strong arms wrapped around his chest, almost pushing him forward with the man’s sudden appearance behind him.

“You were gone for 2 whole months, and all you want to do is talk about books?” The voice was muffled, soft even behind his back.

Phainon’s breathing hitched–the gnawing feeling in his chest rising out of his body, feeling that these affections are not meant for him. He stole them away, he didn’t deserve it; but at the same time, he wanted to indulge in it badly. Would it kill the world for him to even desire even the simplest of joys? Why couldn’t he ask for more ? With everyone’s expectations of him, he felt that it was wrong–when one of his own wishes could have made more space for another’s… He was the hero, the savior, the deliverer of Amphoreus… how could he even…

His spiraling thoughts were cut off when Mydei let him go and turned him around, now the two were face to face–standing eye to eye in front of one another. Mydei didn’t speak, so did Phainon; only the breeze of the wind coming in from the window could be heard.

“Are you not going to say anything?” Mydei started, his face now as red as the flame in his left cheek. “You know what, hks , I’m going to leave-”

“Wait!” Phainon immediately called out and grabbed his hand, pulling Mydei back towards him.

Mydei now stood in front of him once more, those golden eyes glaring at him and his arms crossed, waiting for Phainon to explain himself. Phainon took a deep breath, and raised his hand– almost shaking as Mydei’s eyes followed its movement. Their eyes met and Mydei’s brow shot up.

“He…he,” Phainon awkwardly laughed and let his hand touch the single braid on Mydei’s left shoulder. 

He felt the tensed up man slowly relax his shoulders– wondering what the large white dog in front of him was up to. From the metal clip, up to the thick strands of crimson tips interwoven together, he pressed on them between his fingers and thumb as if his life depended on it. The man in front of him was real; he was standing in front of Mydei– not to kill him, but to appease a lover who has missed their partner dearly from their long absence. He placed his free hand on the other side of Mydei’s neck, his thumb brushing over the burning flames painted over them. 

As the blue horizon met the golden rays of the sun, Phainon brought his face towards Mydei–both their eyes shutting close as their lips finally met with a soft touch. Phainon opened his eyes, moving back, in an attempt to gauge Mydei’s reaction, but was only met with the man’s lips now parted, almost leaning towards Phainon–as if a thirsty man finally given water after a drought only to be suddenly taken away from him. Mydei’s eyes went wide, his face now as red as a ripe tomato over his actions and Phainon couldn’t help but let out a hearty chuckle.

“Y..YOU-!” Before the man could spit out curses, Phainon had now placed both his hands on Mydei’s neck, and quickly planted his lips on the man’s. As if whatever shackled him behind were ruptured, deepening the kiss and forcing entrance on Mydei’s mouth with his tongue.

“Hnggh…!” Mydei moaned, trying to breathe but Phainon’s advances were relentless. Their tongues wrapped around one another, fighting for dominion over another.

The two parted for air, and Phainon’s eyes travelled over the trail of saliva that still connected the two. Both of them were heaving up and down, but from Phainon’s point of view, from the low neckline of Mydei’s garb, the man’s chest was also as red as his tattoos. Mydei’s brows were scrunched up, his eyes sharp and lidded as he looked down, lips parted to catch his breath, and with his arm, tried to wipe the drool spilling from the side of his mouth.

Before the cat could clean up and complain, Phainon pulled Mydei in once more– going with the flow of his instinct, the millions of memories, the hunger and longing all mixing over as he pushed Mydei down on the bed. Phainon put his arms on the sides, framing Mydei in between him– the lion’s mane spread over the white sheets. He parted Mydei’s legs with his knee, and fit himself right in between him. A number of memories played right at the back of his mind, of similar scenes that all lead to the same direction. His kisses were deep and angry– almost burning with hatred and jealousy as he left his mark on every corner of Mydei’s mouth. The number of different Phainons who were able to touch and hold their Mydeis in ways he was never able to with his very own. The way he could be every Phainon that has existed; all his memories, physical features, strengths and weaknesses were all his to own, but Mydeimos’ love was a unique experience to each one of them. One that he can no longer think of ever possessing in his lifetime.

With his thoughts spiraling, Mydei’s small push for wanting to take a breather, made Phainon frantic– a fear of Mydei not wanting him looming over him like a curse. In quick succession, he held Mydei’s wrists and pinned them above his head, trapping the large lion beneath him. He continued his onslaught of kisses, despite Mydei’s efforts to break away. Mydei squirmed underneath Phainon, and with all his strength, bit Phainon’s lips hard enough to draw blood.

“P-Phainon…!” Mydei finally managed to breathe out, and Phainon froze on the spot, like a bucket of cold water just washed over him, realizing what he had done.

In that one single moment of vulnerability, Mydei was able to flip them over, hands now clasping around the throat of the man under him, and strong legs straddling around Phainon’s waist.

“Who are you? ” Mydei’s tone was cold, dangerous; his eyes burning a hole right through Phainon, and his hands clasping around the man’s neck harder as he leaned down.

Locks of golden strands fell forward, cascading down like waterfalls as light spilled through those thin golden crimson strands. Phainon would have reveled in the view if the man on top of him wasn’t currently trying to kill him.

“I-It’s me.. Phainon ..” His voice was light and almost squeaky, as his breath was being slowly taken away from him. Phainon switched between trying to scratch and tap away Mydei’s hands off him, but they remained steady and firm. Tears started to build on the side of his eyes, as he tried gasping for air.

“No, you are not,” Mydei hissed every syllable, his voice unyielding, as if he was not going to accept any other answer.

Could Mydei really tell the difference?

Mydei knew that this man was different, and it sent different mixed signals in his head– confusion, pain, worry, heartbreak… What could have happened on that trip? Was there actually someone strong enough to best his equal? Took his skin and tried to play as his deliverer, stupidly thinking that he could do as he pleased around Mydei. These thoughts only made him furious. The man below him revered him the same way Phainon always would. His face, body, mannerisms, Mydei knew of were all the same, but there was something more that made him uncomfortable; a distress signal blaring, telling him to get away from this man– something ominous that lingers… the sadness, emptiness, exhaustion, and a desperation that Mydei knew was not meant for him. As if the burden Phainon was prophesied to carry has already fallen upon him. Why… How…

Phainon’s eyes rolled back, as if ready to accept his demise; the sides of his face wet with tears, mix of blood and drool dripping from his lips and his furrowed brows calming down. But those icy blue eyes still looked at him with the same yearning and longing that his Phainon shouldn’t have been carrying for him; the man’s hands still holding on to Mydei’s wrists. Mydei’s breath faltered and his grip lightened, setting Phainon up to a coughing fit as he was freed. If he really did lose his Phainon… then he needed some answers. And he will make this man pay for whatever he did.

Mydei kept at his position, kneeling with his hands still close to Phainon, pinning the man’s shoulders down to the bed; ready to attack at any given moment. He watched the man continue coughing, wiping his tears and mouth with the back of his hand.

“I am only letting you go to let you speak. Explain yourself!”

Khaslana looked away, not wanting to look at how the cloth on this man’s chest was also falling down, exposing the shape and lines of his breasts. He thought that this is not really the best time to do a revelation, but he also didn’t know when would actually be the right time… or if there was even such a time. But there was also a mellow feeling in his chest at the sight of Mydei’s controlled rage. If it wasn’t for that, Phainon could have already said goodbye to his head from the moment those hands found their way to his neck. Mydei was this angry for Phainon; but at his core, he was never a man for needless bloodshed. He wanted answers, then the impending bloodshed would no longer be needless.

“I am really going to kill you. Speak before I change my mind.”

Could he even explain all of it to Mydei? Will Mydei believe him? He rubbed at his neck, still feeling the iron grip that once held them. What was he to lose? His initial reaction was simply a pretense to calm Mydei down. Khaslana knew well that he still had a mission to fulfill now that he had taken over this cycle’s Deliverer– and it always took priority more than anything because he knew what was at stake. Much much bigger than anything that they could imagine. But in the end, Mydei was always willing to listen if it came from Phainon; even if his heart and soul could tell that this man was someone who stole his lover’s face.

Khaslana had already sworn to follow through his mission, to discard all these unnecessary feelings, and continue on when he has already reached this far. In the end, all of the heirs were going to die for the prophecy or by his blade; to usher in a new cycle. It only became a matter of Khaslana jumping around the blame. And the man before him, who always stood in his way; always reinforcing what Khaslana has fought for; and every time, Khaslana always stabbed right at Mydei’s 10th thoracic vertebrae. What was a little secret exposed for another cycle to drown out from millions?

“It’s still me…,” Khaslana breathed out, his voice soft, almost a murmur. “... Phainon .”

Mydei only watched him intently, like a hawk ready to attack its prey. Khaslana revealed the truth of the cycles, the true purpose of the flamechase journey, and what Phainon has done in the best summarized way he can offer. If only he could ask Mydei to get off him, but he also enjoyed the feeling of the large man hovering over him. He trapped Khaslana in between his arms, and with his one hand, placed it by Khaslana’s chest–feeling the warmth radiating from it.

“You lived through… how many cycles again?”

“24 802 691,” Khaslana answered.

“That’s… how many coreflames …” Mydei trailed off, trying to compute it in his head.

“297 632 292 coreflames in total,” Khaslana chuckled. “Just like in every cycle, math has never been your strongest suit.”

“I will battle you here and now, and throw you right ahead to the next cycle,” Mydei spat. “Go on, speak!”

“I’m joking, Mydei,” He laughed, and as if from muscle memory to want to hold Mydei in place, his hands landed on both sides of Mydei’s waist.

“Hmmph! You speak as if you have no brain,” Mydei hissed, not minding the uninvited hands now holding him. It was as if any other day he spent with Phainon during a few hours of rest they can steal from their duties.

“Is… my Phainon really gone?” 

“You love to read, Mydei,” Khaslana teased, a wicked smirk on his lips. “What does your literature say about the concept of ‘self’? How would you define your Phainon? Am I not Phainon enough for you?”

“You… this…” Mydei was trying to make sense of things, his thoughts provoked from Phainon’s questioning. The very same man who always had a way with words, a renowned debater with notable awards to his name even. 

It was at that question he realized how did he see Phainon. The Phainon below him was just a Phainon who have just seen it all, and Mydei knew, that at the end of the world, he will love him nonetheless. If he were to think deeper, Mydei is the one at a disadvantage. This Phainon is every Phainon every Mydei have loved in every cycle–even his very own. But this Mydei was just one, one with but a singular memory, one who could never hold a candle to all the Mydeimoses he have met.

He moved back and fell flat on his ass, forgetting that he was still on top of Phainon, making both of their eyes widen in shock. Only when he felt the hard thing pressing on his back did he remember and turned back to Phainon with a deadpan expression.

“Are you serious?”

“Ah, Kephale, I’m sorry,” Khaslana ran his hands over his face and kept them there–a futile attempt to hide his embarrassment. His face was hot and definitely red now from Mydei’s view. “P-Please… please get off me, Mydeimos.”

Mydei bit his lip as he watched the man under him—if what this man is saying is true, then somewhere within this man’s memories was still his own Phainon? But who was he kidding, Phainon will always be Phainon to him. Aside from his people, Mydei had already dedicated himself to Phainon’s cause. He believed in him, his promise and deliverance with his whole heart, and whatever his decisions that lead to this moment, then there must be a greater purpose it serves. 

He tried to lift Khaslana’s arm, wanting to see his face; to which Khaslana only tried to keep in place, turning into a small tug of war between them. Mydei decided to push backward, but might have miscalculated the distance, when he felt Khaslana’s bulge right below his ass. Of course, even in every cycle, the man would obviously have the same body. Khaslana was taken aback, and in an attempt to get Mydei off, he almost slammed his face towards the other as he sat right up. He now locked Mydei in his lap, their chest sticking together with only the fabric of their clothes separating them. The two of them were breathing hard, their chests moving up and down in unison, the rhythm of their heartbeats playing a harmonious tune. Mydei stared at Khaslana’s face–the very same face of the man he loved, the very same eyes he loved–just without the light in them. The burden of the world colored underneath his eyes while an unmistakable fire burned in those irises. This was a man who kept surging through it all despite everything.

His long white strands stuck to his forehead, the ones straying curling around at the edges, his lips wet and red from their kiss, the faint dots that feathered over his flushed cheeks–Mydei couldn’t help but trace his fingers over them, feeling the strange and almost burning heat from his skin. Mydei would have already winced if he wasn’t used to that kind of temperature. Khaslana closed his eyes and leaned in closer to that hand, embracing this feeling that will soon be taken away from him as always. Mydei wrapped his arms around the man’s neck, and their lips met once more. 

Khaslana’s hands started roaming around and as the two parted from the kiss, Mydei now hugged him by his broad shoulders– taking in the familiar scent of his man. Mydei’s grip tightened as soon as he felt those long fingers flutter down his spine and slip under his undergarment.

“With the number of cycles you’ve been through, then you should have done this just as much with my other versions. Should I be concerned...?” Mydei asked, and bit his lips soon after to fight the moans escaping his lips.

"Are you jealous of yourself?" Khaslana’s body vibrated from his chuckle, then he shrugged. “If it helps, not one cycle has it not been you, Mydeimos. Maybe some were luckier or more unfortunate than the others, but you will continue to haunt my days and my nights for all my lives."

Mydei shut his eyes, burying his forehead on the man’s clavicle as tears formed on the side of his eyes.

“So what are you going to do now?”

“I will still… need to do what I have to do,” Khaslana spoke, and Mydei could feel the deep sigh the man had let go. But for once, the man had let his desires speak, “In the meantime, indulge me a little, won’t you?”

How could Mydei ever deny him?

_____________

Khaslana looked at the worn down paper on his hand, scratched his head and checked his surroundings. For some reason, Mydei seemed to want to play around, and left a map for Khaslana to follow. While it was properly labeled, Castrum Kremnos was mostly in ruins to be able to quickly find these landmarks.

After a few more walking, fighting some black tide creatures along the way, as some of the views slowly grew familiar; only then did it dawn on Khaslana on where Mydei wanted to meet him. In the center of a large land surrounded by large lush trees, stood the remains of a tall and proud building. While most of its paint has peeled off, pillars and walls have crumbled, its distinct architecture unique to Kremnos could still be praised by wandering passers-by. 

Phainon entered the main large door that was already open, his boots stepping on dusty and cracked marbled floors. His steps echoed through the empty dark hall, and made his way towards another door that was already open. As he neared, he could already hear the soft clank of metal, a few thuds, grunts and sighs and the momentary shuffling of pages. He entered the room and that one familiar figure he had embedded in his mind for over millions of times came into view. In the middle was a large wooden table with stacks of books, and few others opened with marked pages. Mydei didn’t bother to greet the newcomer, and remained focused on the book that was on the verge of decaying in his hands.

Khaslana couldn't help but chuckle as he approached the man, “Mydeimos, you're so cruel.”

Mydei didn’t budge one bit as Phainon stood behind him. Phainon wrapped his arms around the dip of Mydei’s waist and placed his chin over the man’s shoulder– peeking at the contents of the book that had intrigued the cute large lion so much. The edges of the pages were already dark and torn, with text written in a language that Phainon wasn’t familiar with.

“Call it, a little revenge. You still did take my Phainon away from me,” Mydei shrugged, and Phainon couldn’t help the snort that escaped his lips. The lion now tried to move his head and raised his eyebrow at Phainon. “With every thought that comes into my head about you, I can't help but think if the other Mydeimoses have already thought the same in the past cycles…”

But maybe it didn’t matter. If it was programmed, or some red string of fate, as long as the cycles persist, Mydeimos would always love Phainon in his own way just as the Mydei of the original cycle did. Unfortunately, they were also doomed to separate, to battle until death and for Khaslana to carry all these memories until the end of time.

“I only heard of this grand library from my friends before they departed,” Mydei started, his voice soft, but heavy with longing. Phainon glanced at Mydei’s face and the man simply had his eyes down, his long eyelashes fluttering as he breathed and a faint red on his cheeks. “Before you took my Phainon away, he loved to bring me books from ruins he visited in his solo missions. He has always expressed his intent to learn about my culture too. If things got better, I would have loved to rebuild this library, then show him around. Maybe he'd open up a little about his own home too…”

Mydei sighed, and Khaslana could feel every movement as the two remained attached to one another. The latter realized that despite his straightforward attitude to almost everyone, he has barely revealed any of his past to anyone. But now, he was able to bear his heart open to this one Mydei, out of all the countless Mydeis he never had the chance to.

“I’m just really some ordinary guy from a farming province who wanted to protect his small town,” Khaslana said and smiled-feeling light from admitting such a truth. A simple life, a simple wish, but he also knew the cost that comes with it. “I used to play around with faeries, carve wooden dolls and pretend to be the hero. Compared to the crown prince, who lived a lavish, but stressful royal life, don’t you think we’d make such an interesting couple in a romance book?”

Mydei’s brows furrowed at the mention of the lavish, but it might have been Phainon mixing in some other cycles. He saw no point in correcting him, and instead focused on other matters, “There is no such thing–”

“As romance in the Kremnoan language,” Khaslana continued, and laughed at how Mydei gave him such an incredulous look.

Mydei rolled his eyes, and went back to flipping the pages. 

After a while, he asked, “I wonder, what were my other iterations of this scene?”

Khaslana tightened his hug, and buried his face deeper on the crook of Mydei’s neck, “Just as you thought, they wished I'd visit this library in the next life too…”

“And did you?”

“I…” Khaslana trailed off, his breath lingering on Mydei’s skin, thinking of the number of times this very same library had fallen to flames. 

Because there was no next life for them. It was just a never ending cycle of unfulfilled promises. Maybe he did have the chance to come visit in the next cycle, but the person who invited him was no longer there. There was only a new Mydei, and a new Phainon that he will invite once more. This grand library, a treasure trove of Kremnos’ culture and traditions, history and life that Mydei held dear–a piece of Mydeimos’ heart–that was no longer meant for Khaslana.

“I burned them all.”

He could feel the sudden pause from Mydei–from his breathing to his movement, it was all very clear that Mydei also realized what it meant.

Mydei’s lips parted, and turned around, his hands now holding Phainon’s face, “I didn't expect I would be delivering such a wicked punishment…”

Khaslana simply stole this chance this time around. If the next life really came, he wished–no, he…maybe someday… but then, there really was no point. He can never do this again. He can’t risk it.

“How many cycles has it been again?”

“24 802 691,” Khaslana sighed.

“And how many times have I entrusted my back to you?”

“24 802 691 times.”

“I guess I no longer have to say it anymore,” Mydei let out a hearty laugh and looked at those familiar bright blue eyes that he has always chosen to drown in. “ My one and only weakness. ” 

Either be it his 10th thoracic vertebrae or the man standing in front of him right now, it will be a choice he knows in his heart that his previous versions have never regretted, nor his future iterations will, despite never having their memories. Phainon will be the one choice he will always trust and have faith in.

He grabbed the belt on Khaslana’s chest, and their lips crashed as a number of books came falling down the tiled floors.

But in the end, every cycle must come to an end and start anew.

If it wasn't Flame Reaver, then it was the program that would force them to their destination. The Black Tide will continuously come and worsen to push the heirs to complete their journey. He turned to Mydei who watched with gritted teeth as they lost one heir after another… his willing accomplice through it all.

And here came the time to collect the last coreflame. 

“It is time, Deliverer!”

At this critical juncture, in this moment of vulnerability, Khaslana asked the man in front of him, despite knowing the answer, despite knowing the outcome, “Mydei… listen , please come with me… Together… Together, let's prove... that we're enough to transcend the prophesized fate!”

“How have the other Mydeimoses answered before?”

Khaslana did not speak, and shut his eyes close–his throat parched and chest heavy. Of course . Even with no words, Mydei understood.

“Then my answer is the same,” Mydei growled. “You have to carry on, Khaslana. You at least owe me a proper farewell.”

Just as countless other cycles before, Khaslana watched Mydeimos transform into the Lance of Fury. Khaslana clutched his chest and transformed as well, a proper match and duel between him and his lover of millions of cycles. Despite the number of cycles, not once was he able to bring anyone to the next one; he was always destined to be alone. Their fate… their prophecy –their duty always takes priority no matter what.

And just like any other duel that came before them, the ending remains the same. Phainon combed his shaking fingers through Mydei’s long bangs, wanting to embed the man’s face in his mind one more time, but at the cost of also subjecting himself to see the light in those eyes falter away by the minute. Golden blood dripped down from Mydei’s lips… down to his chest, as the Dawnmaker was buried deep into his back. Beads of tears formed on the sides of Phainon's eyes, evaporating before they could even fall as he cradled the dying Mydeimos in his arms–his tattered wings caging the two of them from the uncaring eyes of fate. 

Phainon wailed loudly, repeatedly calling Mydei’s name like a prayer; crying that he didn’t want to be left alone. Hearing Phainon like this broke Mydei’s heart beyond repair. It was as if his heart was being squeezed and twisted like cloth, run over by thousands of dromas–hurting more than the actual sword lodged on his spine. He was used to physical pain, he can die ten thousand times, but it doesn't compare one bit to how he’s feeling now; watching the man he loves break down like this. He wished he could try to hush his tears down, but he knew it was useless. Mydei was going to die, and Phainon will have to continue on; it was a fate they cannot fight or run from.

Mydei smiled at Phainon, hoping that one day both of them– no , all of them, can finally rest, and maybe, even have the chance to fulfill their own wishes. If given the chance… to see Phainon again in the next life at his library. He spent all his remaining strength to reach Phainon, to caress his face tenderly one last time.

“Go forward, Deliverer, and I’ll meet you there once more.”
